properties.name: Lucali
properties.blurb: A converted candy store turned into one of the city's most sought-after coal-oven pies. No slices, cash only, and a line that starts before opening — reserve ahead or plan to wait.

properties.name: Di Fara Pizza
properties.blurb: The benchmark by which a lot of NYC pizza gets judged. Founder Dom DeMarco built the reputation over decades; the family runs it today with the same hand-snipped basil finish.

properties.name: Grimaldi's
properties.blurb: A DUMBO fixture since 1990, cooking coal-oven pies with a thin, blistered crust in the shadow of the Brooklyn Bridge. One of the pizzerias most credited with starting the modern NYC pizza pilgrimage.

properties.name: Juliana's
properties.blurb: Opened in 2012 by Patsy Grimaldi in the very space where he first started. Same coal oven, same thin char-edged crust; regulars debate endlessly which DUMBO neighbor is better.

properties.name: Table 87
properties.blurb: Brooklyn Heights spot billing itself as the first in the borough to offer coal-oven pizza by the slice. Thin, charred crust with a crisp undercarriage — a solid stop near DUMBO.

properties.name: Totonno's
properties.blurb: Open since 1924 in Coney Island, one of the oldest coal-oven pizzerias in the country. Cash only, whole pies only, still run by the founder's descendants.

properties.name: L&B Spumoni Gardens – Gravesend
properties.blurb: A Gravesend institution since the late 1930s, known for its upside-down square slices — sauce on top, cheese on the bottom — and the spumoni ice cream that gives the place its name.

properties.name: L'Industrie Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Williamsburg slice shop built around one standout order: a fior di latte square topped with cold burrata and basil after it comes out of the oven. Expect a line most evenings.

properties.name: Ops
properties.blurb: A Bushwick spot building long-fermented sourdough pies in a low-key setting. Seasonal toppings and a natural wine list — closer to a Brooklyn supper club than a traditional pizzeria.

properties.name: Wheated
properties.blurb: A Ditmas Park neighborhood spot serving sourdough-crust pies with craft beer, drawing a loyal local crowd far from the usual pizza-pilgrimage circuit.

properties.name: Giuseppina's
properties.blurb: Run by the brother of Lucali's founder, widely cited as the closest thing to Lucali for those who can't get a reservation. Thin brick-oven pies in a small South Slope dining room.

properties.name: Luigi's Pizza
properties.blurb: A South Slope cash-only slice counter that's been going since the 1970s. The kind of unfussy neighborhood joint that regulars defend fiercely and tourists rarely find.

properties.name: Sottocasa
properties.blurb: A Boerum Hill wood-fired Neapolitan spot set a few steps below street level, with an oven imported from Naples and the soft-centered, leopard-spotted crust the style demands.

properties.name: Speedy Romeo
properties.blurb: A Michelin Bib Gourmand winner out of a former auto shop in Clinton Hill. The pizzas veer from Italian into Midwestern bar-pie territory — the St. Louis with Provel cheese and pickled peppers is the one to order.

properties.name: Best Pizza
properties.blurb: A Williamsburg spot best known for its grandma slice — crushed tomato, garlic, and a hit of chopped anchovy under a well-browned, lacy-crisp bottom crust.

properties.name: The Astarita
properties.blurb: A Carroll Gardens counter serving old-school NY slices in a no-frills setting. One of those neighborhood joints that's never made a list but has been quietly feeding the same block for years.

properties.name: Brooklyn DOP
properties.blurb: A Park Slope Neapolitan spot using DOP-certified Italian ingredients with a wood-fired oven and a neighborhood-restaurant feel that's more relaxed than the destination-pizza circuit.

properties.name: F&F Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Carroll Gardens square-slice spot with a loyal local following — reliable, well-charred Sicilian squares from a no-frills counter that rarely makes headlines but always delivers.

properties.name: Patsy's Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Brooklyn outpost of the Harlem original, one of NYC's oldest coal-oven operations. Thin, light, blistered pies in a classic red-sauce dining room setting.

properties.name: Lucky Charlie
properties.blurb: A Bushwick slice shop that's earned a neighborhood following for its straightforward NY-style slices in an area otherwise better known for sourdough and natural-wine pies.

properties.name: Frankie's of Bay Ridge
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge neighborhood staple serving the kind of large, foldable NY slices that define the outer-borough pizza experience — nothing flashy, just consistently good.

properties.name: Joe's Pizza
properties.blurb: The Greenwich Village original, open since 1975. No frills, fold-and-go, and about as close to a citywide consensus pick for classic NY slice as exists.

properties.name: Prince Street Pizza
properties.blurb: The spicy spring pepperoni square, curled and crisped at the edges, is the reason for the perpetual Nolita line. Get there off-peak if you don't want to wait.

properties.name: Lombardi's
properties.blurb: Widely recognized as America's first pizzeria, open since 1905 in Little Italy. Coal-oven pies served whole (no slices), with fresh mozzarella and San Marzano tomato simplicity that makes the history feel earned.

properties.name: Scarr's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Lower East Side slice shop that mills some of its own wheat in the basement daily. The result is a noticeably nuttier crust on what is otherwise a classic NY slice — the New Yorker called it one of the best in the city.

properties.name: Una Pizza Napoletana
properties.blurb: Anthony Mangieri's obsessively focused Lower East Side operation: a short fixed menu of wood-fired Neapolitan pies, open only a few days a week, with a national reputation built over decades.

properties.name: John's of Bleecker Street
properties.blurb: A West Village institution since 1929, with a coal oven that turns out thin, blistered whole pies only — no slices, no delivery. The original booths and brick walls have barely changed.

properties.name: Song' E Napule
properties.address: 132 W Houston St, New York, NY 10012
properties.blurb: A Greenwich Village Neapolitan with a Michelin Bib Gourmand, known for its lighter, airier crust and a dining room that feels more neighborhood trattoria than destination pizzeria.

properties.name: Don Antonio
properties.blurb: Roberto Caporuscio's Midtown Neapolitan. The montanara (fried then baked) is the signature, but the classic wood-fired pies hold their own.

properties.name: Lucia Pizza of SoHo
properties.blurb: A SoHo slice window turning out a consistently excellent classic slice — understated compared to trendier neighbors, but a reliable go-to for anyone in the area.

properties.name: L'Industrie West Village
properties.blurb: The Manhattan sibling of the Williamsburg original, bringing the same burrata-topped slice to the West Village. Same lines, same quality, slightly easier to reach from Midtown.

properties.name: Lazzara's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Garment District lunchtime institution since 1978, up a narrow staircase to a second-floor dining room. Thick, focaccia-style squares that have fueled the neighborhood for decades.

properties.name: Capizzi
properties.blurb: A Hell's Kitchen wood-fired spot that flies under the radar, turning out solid Neapolitan pies in a low-key setting without the usual Midtown tourist markup.

properties.name: Joe & Pat's
properties.blurb: A Staten Island institution since 1960, known for its cracker-thin crust with a secret Neapolitan recipe in the family since the founders came over from Naples.

properties.name: Denino's
properties.address: 524 Port Richmond Ave, Staten Island, NY 10302
properties.blurb: Open since 1937 with the motto 'In crust we trust,' Denino's is the Staten Island bar pie benchmark — thin, crispy, tavern-style pies in a neighborhood bar that's barely changed in decades.

properties.name: Lee's Tavern
properties.blurb: A Dongan Hills corner bar with no sign and no website — you have to know to look for it. The thin, crispy bar pies are among the best on the island, and the cash-only, regulars-first vibe is entirely genuine.

properties.name: Goodfella's
properties.blurb: A brick-oven Staten Island staple best known for its vodka pie — rich, creamy, and consistently well-executed. One of the borough's most recommended spots for anyone visiting from outside.

properties.name: Rizzo's Fine Pizza
properties.blurb: An Astoria square-slice institution since the 1950s — thick, cheese-forward, and sauced on top in the old-school style. A neighborhood staple that draws people from across the borough.

properties.name: Andrew Bellucci's Pizzeria
properties.blurb: Founded by the late Andrew Bellucci, widely called the 'Don of Dough,' and still going strong in Astoria after his passing in 2023. The fresh-shucked clam pie is the signature; the classic NY slice holds up too.

properties.name: New Park Pizza
properties.address: 156-71 Cross Bay Blvd, Howard Beach, NY 11414
properties.blurb: A Howard Beach institution since 1956, right on the way to JFK. Salt sprinkled on the oven floor before each pie produces a uniquely crispy, flavorful crust — regulars order it well-done.

properties.name: Brooklyn Firefly
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge wood-fired spot with a neighborhood-restaurant feel — seasonal ingredients, a carefully tended dough, and the kind of low-key atmosphere that keeps locals coming back without much fanfare.

properties.name: DaVinci Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Bensonhurst neighborhood slice counter on 18th Avenue — one of Brooklyn's most authentically Italian-American commercial strips. Classic NY slices from a spot that's fed the neighborhood for years.

properties.name: J&V Pizzeria
properties.blurb: Another Bensonhurst 18th Avenue staple, a few blocks from DaVinci. The kind of no-frills, cash-friendly corner pizzeria that defines outer-borough slice culture — regulars know the staff by name.

properties.name: Zero Otto Nove
properties.blurb: Named after the area code of owner Roberto Paciullo's hometown of Salerno, this Arthur Avenue trattoria is the most celebrated pizza destination in the Bronx. Wood-fired pies with a puffy Sorrento-style crust, sourcing mozzarella from the legendary Casa della Mozzarella down the block.

properties.name: Louie & Ernie's
properties.blurb: A Bronx classic since 1959 in the Schuylerville neighborhood — pizza and calzones only, no frills, no extras. Named one of the best hole-in-the-wall restaurants in New York State, and a perennial pick on every serious Bronx pizza list.

properties.name: Pugsley Pizza
properties.blurb: A Belmont neighborhood staple since 1984, right near the Bronx Zoo and Botanical Garden. Super-cheesy thin-crust slices in a lively, graffiti-covered room — a reliably great stop before or after an afternoon in the park.

properties.name: Patricia's
properties.blurb: A Michelin-listed brick-oven trattoria in Morris Park, more convivial and elegant than most Bronx pizza spots. The Regina — buffalo mozzarella, torn basil, and olive oil — is the one to order.

properties.name: Nick's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Forest Hills neighborhood institution since 1993, consistently rated the best pizza in Queens by both critics and locals. Fresh mozzarella pulled in-house, thin charred crust, whole pies only — cash only. Order the margherita.

properties.name: Philomena's
properties.blurb: A Sunnyside neighborhood spot that's built a loyal Queens following for its light, carefully fermented dough and a square pie that Kelly Ripa called out by name on live TV. Family-run, unpretentious, and genuinely excellent.

properties.name: Pizza Wagon
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge slice counter with a neighborhood following — no frills, just consistent NY-style pies from a spot that's been feeding the local crowd for years.

properties.name: Rosa's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Ridgewood neighborhood slice counter right on the Queens-Brooklyn border, serving the kind of no-frills, satisfying NY slice that the surrounding Italian-American community has relied on for years.

properties.name: Mano's Pizzeria
properties.blurb: An Astoria slice shop with a loyal following for its classic NY-style pies. Low-key, consistent, and the kind of place where regulars don't need to look at the menu.

properties.name: Chrissy's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Greenpoint corner slice shop beloved by the neighborhood for its consistent classic NY slices. No frills, cash-friendly, and the kind of place you stop at on the way home.

properties.name: Dellarocco's
properties.blurb: A Brooklyn Heights neighborhood pizzeria with a wood-fired oven and a warm, convivial dining room. Solid Neapolitan pies with quality ingredients, a reliable wine list, and a loyal local following.

properties.name: Il Porto
properties.blurb: A Clinton Hill wood-fired Neapolitan spot tucked away on Washington Avenue, with a neighborhood-restaurant feel and a menu that goes well beyond pizza into proper Italian fare.

properties.name: Nino's
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge institution that's been doing old-school NY slices for decades. The neighborhood has changed around it; Nino's hasn't — and that's exactly the point.

properties.name: Pizza Secret
properties.blurb: A Park Slope slice counter with a name that undersells it — the 'secret' is a reliably good classic NY slice in a neighborhood that's increasingly hard to find one without a wait or a concept attached.

properties.name: Table 87 – 3rd Avenue
properties.blurb: The second Table 87 location, bringing the same coal-oven slice concept to the Gowanus/Park Slope border. Same crispy, char-edged crust as the Atlantic Ave original, more convenient for south Brooklyn.

properties.name: Fini Pizza
properties.blurb: A Williamsburg slice window that's become a neighborhood staple for its straightforward, well-executed NY slices. A no-fuss alternative to the more elaborate pizza concepts that have multiplied in the neighborhood.

properties.name: Diamond Slice
properties.blurb: A Greenpoint slice counter with a following for its large, well-sauced NY slices. Exactly what the name suggests — a reliable diamond in a neighborhood that keeps getting more expensive around it.

properties.name: Kesté Pizza & Vino
properties.blurb: Roberto Caporuscio's Financial District outpost of the celebrated Neapolitan operation (the Bleecker Street original closed in 2021). New York Magazine and Food Network Magazine have both named Kesté the best pizza in New York — the wood-fired pies with DOP-certified ingredients make a strong case.

properties.name: Gnocco
properties.blurb: An East Village Italian restaurant named after the fried dough snack, with a wood-fired oven turning out Neapolitan pies in a warm, candlelit dining room. One of the neighborhood's most consistently recommended Italian spots.

properties.name: Arturo's Coal Oven Pizza
properties.address: 106 W Houston St, New York, NY 10012
properties.blurb: A Greenwich Village coal-oven institution since 1957, with live jazz most nights and a dining room that looks like it hasn't changed since then. The pies are thin, coal-kissed, and served whole — the experience is as much of the point as the pizza.

properties.name: Cello's Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Lower East Side slice counter with a neighborhood following for its classic NY slices at a price point that's increasingly hard to find downtown. No frills, consistent, and reliably good.

properties.name: Brothers Pizza
properties.address: 750 Port Richmond Ave, Staten Island, NY 10302
properties.blurb: A Port Richmond slice counter not far from Denino's, serving the kind of reliable, no-frills NY-style slices that make this corner of Staten Island one of the borough's best pizza neighborhoods.

properties.name: Ungaro Coal Fired Pizza Cafe
properties.blurb: A coal-fired Staten Island spot on Forest Avenue serving thin, blistered pies at high heat. One of the borough's more distinctive pizza options for those who want something beyond the classic bar-pie and slice-joint circuit.

properties.name: Tommy's Pizza
properties.blurb: An old-school Throggs Neck slice joint with a cash-only policy, a cornmeal-dusted crust that comes out uniquely crispy, and the kind of no-frills atmosphere where the pizza does the talking. A Bronx East Side staple for decades.

properties.name: La Villa
properties.blurb: A Dyker Heights neighborhood restaurant with a wood-fired oven and a loyal following that stretches well beyond the immediate neighborhood. Known for its thin, properly charred pies and a full Italian menu — one of the better-kept secrets in southern Brooklyn.

properties.name: Amore Pizza
properties.blurb: A Flushing neighborhood pizzeria serving classic NY-style slices in one of Queens' most diverse and food-rich neighborhoods. A local staple that holds its own in a part of the borough better known for its international food scene.

properties.name: The Square on Annadale
properties.blurb: An Annadale neighborhood staple built around the authentic Sicilian square pie — thick, cheese-forward, and sauced on top in the upside-down style. One of the south shore's most consistent and welcoming spots, with a friendly owner and a loyal regulars crowd.

properties.name: La Vera Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A neighborhood favorite on Clove Road that quickly built a following for its thin-crust pies after taking over a beloved spot that had closed. Consistently praised for delivering a great slice in a part of Staten Island that was missing one.

properties.name: Mimmo's Brick Oven Pizza
properties.blurb: A family-owned Great Kills trattoria with a real brick oven fired by NY oak wood at 650°F. Creative specialty pies — the clam, the steak and caramelized onion, the cup-and-char honey pie — in a full Italian dining room with a warm, rustic southern Italian atmosphere.

properties.name: Nonna's
properties.blurb: A Tottenville neighborhood pizzeria at the southernmost tip of Staten Island — and arguably of all of New York City. The kind of local institution where regulars know the staff and the menu hasn't changed much in years, which is exactly the point.

properties.name: Lucia Pizza of Avenue X
properties.blurb: A Sheepshead Bay neighborhood slice counter on Avenue X — deep southern Brooklyn, far off the tourist circuit. Solid classic NY slices in a no-frills setting that's been feeding the neighborhood for years.

properties.name: Nonna's Pizza Great Kills
properties.blurb: A Great Kills neighborhood pizzeria tucked away on Brower Court — the kind of local spot that doesn't need a sign out front because the regulars already know where it is.

properties.name: Upside Pizza – Spring St
properties.blurb: The SoHo location of Upside Pizza — same upside-down concept as the original, with cheese caramelized against the crust and sauce on top. A reliably satisfying slice in an area that's not known for them.

properties.name: Upside Pizza – Greenpoint
properties.blurb: The Greenpoint outpost of Upside Pizza, bringing the flipped-slice concept to Brooklyn. Cheese-bottom, sauce-top, crackly crust — a fun change of pace from classic NY-style.

properties.name: Upside Pizza – Broadway
properties.blurb: The Upper West Side Upside Pizza — same upside-down slice as the other locations, in a neighborhood that needed a good slice window.

properties.name: APizza – Dyker Heights
properties.blurb: A New Haven-style apizza outpost in Dyker Heights — long-fermented dough, high-heat coal-fired oven, and the kind of thin, charred, slightly chewy crust that the Connecticut style is known for. A welcome outlier in southern Brooklyn.

properties.name: Mama's TOO! – West Village
properties.address: 176 Seventh Ave S, New York, NY 10014
properties.blurb: An institution with a cult following for its square slice — thick, airy, well-sauced — and a long list of classic NY pies that deliver without gimmick.

properties.name: Mama's TOO! – Upper West Side
properties.blurb: An institution with a cult following for its square slice — thick, airy, well-sauced — and a long list of classic NY pies that deliver without gimmick.

properties.name: APizza – Dyker 13th Ave
properties.blurb: A Dyker Heights New Haven-style apizza spot — long-fermented dough, coal-fired oven, and the kind of thin, charred, chewy crust that the Connecticut style is known for. A welcome outlier in southern Brooklyn.

properties.name: Patsy's
properties.blurb: The Gramercy Park location of the storied Patsy's brand — one of New York's oldest coal-oven pizzeria lineages, dating back to East Harlem in 1933. Thin, blistered, coal-fired pies with the old-school New York DNA intact.

properties.name: L&B Spumoni Gardens – DUMBO
properties.blurb: The DUMBO outpost of the Gravesend original, bringing the same upside-down Sicilian square — sauce on top, cheese caramelized on the bottom — to one of Brooklyn's busiest tourist corridors.

properties.name: My Pie Pizzeria Romana
properties.blurb: A Midtown East Roman-style pizzeria — thin, crispy, rectangular pies cut with scissors, served by weight. A completely different animal from the NY round pie but worth knowing about.

properties.name: Lucia Pizza of UES
properties.blurb: The Upper East Side outpost of Lucia Pizza, consistent and reliable for a classic NY slice in a neighborhood that can be hit or miss for pizza.

properties.name: Village Square Pizza – Upper East Side
properties.blurb: A neighborhood slice staple on the Upper East Side — consistent NY-style slices that the local crowd relies on.

properties.name: Village Square Pizza – Upper West Side
properties.blurb: The Upper West Side location of Village Square Pizza, a reliable neighborhood slice spot on Broadway.

properties.name: Upside Pizza – 40th St
properties.blurb: Another Upside Pizza location near Grand Central — same flipped-slice concept with cheese caramelized on the bottom and sauce on top.

properties.name: Village Square Pizza – Midtown
properties.blurb: The Midtown West location of Village Square Pizza, a dependable stop for a classic NY slice in the Garment District.

properties.name: Ledo Pizza
properties.blurb: A Garment District slice counter with a loyal lunch crowd — no-frills NY slices at a fair price in one of Midtown's busiest corridors.

properties.name: Square Pizza NYC
properties.blurb: A Times Square-adjacent Sicilian square specialist — thick, cheesy, crispy-bottomed squares in an area otherwise dominated by tourist traps.

properties.name: Joe & Pat's NYC
properties.blurb: A Manhattan outpost of the beloved Staten Island institution, bringing the same cracker-thin crust and Neapolitan family recipe to the East Village.

properties.name: Pizza Loves Sauce
properties.address: 147 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002
properties.blurb: A Lower East Side slice counter known for generously sauced pies — the name says it all. Casual, quick, reliably good.

properties.name: Ceres
properties.blurb: A Nolita wood-fired spot with a focused menu and natural wine list. Seasonal and ingredient-driven — closer to a restaurant than a pizzeria, but the pies are serious.

properties.name: Slicehaus Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A West Village slice shop just a block from Joe's on Carmine Street — bold, well-sauced slices with a loyal neighborhood following.

properties.name: Bleecker Street Pizza
properties.blurb: A Village institution frequently cited alongside Joe's in debates about the best slice in the neighborhood. The Nonna Maria white slice has its own devoted following.

properties.name: Paulie Gee's East Village Slice Shop
properties.blurb: The East Village outpost of the Paulie Gee's slice operation — same old-school NY slice philosophy as the Greenpoint original, now in Manhattan.

properties.name: Paulie Gee's Slice Shop
properties.blurb: The Greenpoint original — simple, old-school New York slices including a solid Sicilian square from the team behind the Paulie Gee's brand.

properties.name: Williamsburg Pizza
properties.blurb: A Williamsburg slice shop that built its name on grandma squares and a full rotation of classic NY pies.

properties.name: Fini Pizza – Barclays
properties.blurb: The Downtown Brooklyn/Barclays location of Fini Pizza — same well-executed NY slices, convenient for anyone catching a game at the arena.

properties.name: Delmar Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Sheepshead Bay neighborhood staple serving classic NY slices in one of Brooklyn's most authentic remaining Italian-American enclaves.

properties.name: Fazio's
properties.blurb: A Bushwick slice counter on Knickerbocker Avenue with a neighborhood following — no-frills, reliable, and the kind of place that's been feeding the block for years.

properties.name: Dani's House of Pizza
properties.blurb: A Kew Gardens institution going back decades — thin-crust pies with a devoted local following and a reputation as one of the best slices in the borough.

properties.name: Louie's
properties.blurb: An Elmhurst neighborhood staple with a loyal following for its classic NY slices in one of Queens' most diverse and underrated food neighborhoods.

properties.name: Milkflower
properties.blurb: An Astoria wood-fired Neapolitan spot with a craft beer selection and a commitment to quality ingredients. One of the borough's most celebrated pizza destinations before a period of closure — confirm open status before visiting.

properties.name: Joe & John's Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Ridgewood neighborhood pizzeria on Myrtle Avenue with a solid local following for its consistent NY-style slices.

properties.name: Sam's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Kingsbridge neighborhood slice counter in the northwest Bronx — reliable, no-frills, and a staple for the local community.

properties.name: Loretta's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Throggs Neck neighborhood pizzeria with a loyal local following — the kind of spot that's been part of the community fabric for years.

properties.name: Salvatores of Riverdale
properties.blurb: A Riverdale neighborhood institution — old-school NY slices in one of the Bronx's most suburban and overlooked neighborhoods for pizza.

properties.name: Venezia Pizza
properties.blurb: A northeast Bronx neighborhood pizzeria with a consistent following for its classic NY-style slices in the Pelham Parkway area.

properties.name: Addeo's
properties.blurb: A Morris Park staple not far from Patricia's — another piece of the Bronx's deep Italian-American pizza tradition, serving the neighborhood for decades.

properties.name: Salvatore's of Soho
properties.blurb: A Riverdale Italian restaurant with a wood-fired oven, serving Neapolitan-style pies in one of the Bronx's most affluent neighborhoods. A cut above the typical Bronx slice joint in terms of ingredients and atmosphere.

properties.name: Rosario's
properties.blurb: A beloved Astoria neighborhood institution serving wood-fired Neapolitan pies to a loyal local following. One of those spots that earns its reputation through consistency and community rather than food media attention.

properties.name: Figlia
properties.blurb: A newer Astoria wood-fired spot just steps from Rosario's on 31st Street, bringing a more modern approach to Neapolitan pizza with creative seasonal toppings and a natural wine list.

properties.name: VIPizza
properties.blurb: A Bayside neighborhood staple on Bell Boulevard, one of Queens' most lively commercial strips. Reliable classic NY slices in a part of the borough with serious pizza roots.

properties.name: Pizza Garden
properties.blurb: A Flushing neighborhood slice shop on Northern Boulevard, serving the Queens community with classic NY-style pies in an area better known for its international food scene.

properties.name: Lucia Pizza Flushing
properties.blurb: A Lucia Pizza outpost right on Roosevelt Avenue in the heart of Flushing, bringing classic NY slices to one of Queens' most diverse and food-rich corridors.

properties.name: Elegante Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge 5th Avenue slice shop with a neighborhood following. Clean, reliable NY-style pies in a stretch of Brooklyn that takes its pizza seriously.

properties.name: Vesuvio Restaurant & Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge Italian-American trattoria named after the volcano that defines Naples — fitting for a place serving wood-fired pies in one of Brooklyn's most Italian neighborhoods. Full restaurant menu alongside the pizza.

properties.name: La Bella Pizza Express
properties.blurb: An 86th Street neighborhood slice counter in Bensonhurst, serving the local Italian-American community with classic NY pies at the right price.

properties.name: Grotta Azzurra
properties.blurb: A Bensonhurst neighborhood pizzeria on 21st Avenue, named after the famous Blue Grotto of Capri. Classic NY slices with the Italian-American roots that define the surrounding neighborhood.

properties.name: Pino Pizza
properties.blurb: A Bath Avenue neighborhood slice shop in Bensonhurst, feeding the local community with reliable classic NY-style pies. The kind of spot you walk to, not drive to.

properties.name: Mamma Mia Pizza
properties.blurb: A Bath Beach neighborhood pizzeria at the edge of southern Brooklyn, where the Italian-American community runs deep and the pizza standards are set accordingly.

properties.name: Knapp Street Pizza
properties.blurb: A Marine Park / Sheepshead Bay neighborhood slice counter on Knapp Street, tucked in one of Brooklyn's most residential southern neighborhoods. A reliable local go-to.

properties.name: Mancini's Wood-Fired Pizza
properties.blurb: A Bay Ridge wood-fired spot on 5th Avenue bringing Neapolitan-style pies to one of Brooklyn's most Italian-American neighborhoods. Housemade dough, quality ingredients, neighborhood-trattoria feel.

properties.name: Espresso Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A Fort Hamilton 5th Avenue slice shop at the southern end of Bay Ridge, serving the neighborhood with solid classic NY-style pies near the Brooklyn-Staten Island border.

properties.name: Maria's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Dyker Heights neighborhood pizzeria on Fort Hamilton Parkway, serving the surrounding Italian-American community with the kind of straightforward classic slice the neighborhood demands.

properties.name: Bad Boys Pizza
properties.blurb: An 80th Street Bensonhurst slice counter with a name that overpromises and a slice that actually delivers. A neighborhood staple for locals who know where to go.

properties.name: Krispy Pizza
properties.blurb: A Dyker Heights neighborhood slice counter on 13th Avenue, in the heart of one of Brooklyn's most Italian-American communities. The name says it all — known for a well-crisped crust and reliable classic NY-style slices.

properties.name: Ace's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Williamsburg neighborhood slice shop on Driggs Avenue with a local following for its no-frills classic NY-style pies. A reliable option in a neighborhood that's increasingly harder to find a straightforward slice.

properties.name: Briciola Pizza Bar
properties.blurb: A West Village wine bar and Neapolitan pizza spot on Bedford Street, one of the neighborhood's most charming blocks. Roman-style thin-crust pies alongside a well-curated wine list — the kind of place that's equally good for a date or a casual weeknight dinner.

properties.name: Fermento Pizza NYC
properties.blurb: A Hudson Square fermentation-focused pizza spot that takes its dough seriously — long cold fermentation, carefully sourced ingredients, and a wood-fired oven. The name is the whole philosophy.

properties.name: Seppe Pizza Bar – Staten Island
properties.address: 3 Navy Pier Ct, Staten Island, NY 10304
properties.blurb: A Staten Island waterfront pizza bar serving wood-fired Neapolitan pies with views of the harbor. One of the more distinctive dining settings on the island — good pizza in an unexpected location.

properties.name: Seppe Pizza Bar – Manhattan
properties.blurb: The Manhattan outpost of Seppe Pizza Bar in Battery Park City, serving wood-fired Neapolitan pies in a neighborhood that's more residential than most of Lower Manhattan.

properties.name: Sotto Le Stelle
properties.address: 44-07 Queens Blvd, Long Island City, NY 11104
properties.blurb: A Long Island City Neapolitan spot on Queens Boulevard bringing wood-fired pies to a neighborhood that's grown rapidly in recent years. A welcome addition to the LIC dining scene.

properties.name: Lenny & John's Pizza
properties.blurb: A Flatbush neighborhood slice counter that's been a local staple for years. Reliable NY-style pies in a part of Brooklyn that takes its corner pizzeria seriously.

properties.name: Tony's Pizzeria
properties.blurb: A 13th Avenue Dyker Heights slice shop with a neighborhood following. Classic NY pies in one of Brooklyn's most Italian-American corridors.

properties.name: Bklyn's Pizza
